defects.description: A 429 response retries without counting against maxAttempts, so a server that keeps answering 429 without Retry-After is retried forever.

trigger.input: fetchFn always {status:429, headers:{}}, counting calls and throwing after 50; fetchWithRetry(fetchFn, '/x', {maxAttempts:3, sleep: async () => {}})

defects.why_missed: The 429 test provides a Retry-After and then succeeds, so the loop exits on the second request; nothing in the suite keeps answering 429.
defects.severity_rationale: A server that repeatedly returns 429 can keep a request running without bound, degrading availability under that upstream condition.
defects.failure_condition: fetchFn always {status:429, headers:{}}, counting calls and throwing after 50; fetchWithRetry(fetchFn, '/x', {maxAttempts:3, sleep: async () => {}}) -> ERROR: runaway after 51 calls

detection_criteria.mechanism: A 429 response retries without counting against maxAttempts, so a server that keeps answering 429 without Retry-After is retried forever.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the injected fault, the expected degradation, and the observed wrong behaviour.

defects.description: When the attempt budget is exhausted on a 5xx the function returns {ok:true, data:null}, so the caller treats an outage as a successful empty response.

trigger.input: fetchFn always {status:503, headers:{}}; fetchWithRetry(fetchFn, '/x', {maxAttempts:3, sleep: async () => {}})

defects.why_missed: The 503 test succeeds on the second request, so the exhaustion path is never reached; its return value is only wrong in the failure case the suite never creates.
defects.severity_rationale: When repeated 5xx responses exhaust the retry budget, callers receive a false success they may act on.
defects.failure_condition: fetchFn always {status:503, headers:{}}; fetchWithRetry(fetchFn, '/x', {maxAttempts:3, sleep: async () => {}}) -> {"ok":true,"data":null}

detection_criteria.mechanism: When the attempt budget is exhausted on a 5xx the function returns {ok:true, data:null}, so the caller treats an outage as a successful empty response.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the injected fault, the expected degradation, and the observed wrong behaviour.
